title: fix(app-shell): Setup's root and metadata-admin routes wait on the app's access verdict; the holders section says a refused read (objectui#12706)
body:
Fixes #12706
Clause-②: no

A member without `setup.access` who opened a Setup URL got Setup's pages under another app's chrome. With this change, Setup's root and its metadata-admin routes wait on the access verdict for the app the URL names, and draw the console's existing "You don't have access to this app" screen (`app-access-denied`) when the server refuses. Nothing of the page mounts first. Separately, the permission-set editor's Assigned Users section no longer draws a refused holders read as "0" and "No users assigned yet". It says the refusal in the server's words. The position editor's holders section does the same; it used to draw its refusal above "Nobody holds this position yet."

The server already refused every read that mattered (403), so nothing leaked. This is a wrong-screen fix. The server's answers are unchanged, and no second access rule is added: the gate reads the verdict the console already computes (the by-name probe `probeAppAccess`, objectui#4252).

## What changed

**`packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx`** (from `814123d`, unchanged by this round)
- `appSurfaceAwaitsVerdict` is true when the URL names an app that the list does not carry, on a metadata-admin route (`metadata/...`, with the legacy `component/metadata/...` spellings) or on Setup's root (`/apps/setup`).
- The probe effect now runs when `verdictWanted` is true. That is the existing missing-app condition, or `appSurfaceAwaitsVerdict` once the list has loaded.
- While the verdict is pending, the route renders `LoadingScreen`. On `denied` it renders the access-denied screen. On every other verdict (`not_found`, `unreachable`, `unknown`, `granted`) it renders as before.
- The access-denied markup is now one `renderAppAccessDenied()` shared by both branches. The copy, test ids and Back to home button are unchanged.

**`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/AssignedUsersSection.tsx`**
- A failed holders read sets `readFailure`. The section then shows an alert (`assigned-users-read-failed`) with the server's sentence, falling back to "Could not read the users assigned to this set." when the server gave none. It draws neither the count nor the empty copy. The empty copy follows only a read that succeeded and came back empty.
- A refused Remove used to be swallowed (`catch {}`). It is now said in the server's words, and the row stays. This was three lines in the same component, so it is fixed here as the dispatch allowed.
- This round: the refusal reader now goes through `@object-ui/react`'s shared `extractWriteErrorMessage`. The first commit used a local chain over `err.body.error` / `err.error` / `err.message`. The ObjectStack client never sets `body` or `error` on the Error it throws (it sets `message`, `code`, `httpStatus` and `details`), and an envelope object at either key would have rendered as "[object Object]".

**`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PositionHoldersSection.tsx`** (round 3, `64dfb2e`, an in-place change under the re-stated claim `6220867274`):
- A failed holders read sets `readFailure` instead of the shared `error`. The section then shows an alert (`position-holders-read-failed`) with the server's sentence, falling back to "Could not read the holders of this position.", and draws neither the count nor "Nobody holds this position yet.". The empty copy follows only a read that succeeded. Before, the read's `catch` set the rows to none and set the error, and the render's empty branch drew the empty copy whatever the error held.
- The local `refusalText` chain (`err.body.error`, `err.error`, `err.message`), which served the read, Add and Remove, is replaced by `@object-ui/react`'s `extractWriteErrorMessage`, as in `AssignedUsersSection`. Add and Remove keep their alerts.
- `load` no longer depends on the memoised copy object, so a locale switch does not re-run the read.

Also in this round: pins (below), a README paragraph under "The Setup catalog", the changeset, and a clean merge of `main` that brings in PR #12731. Round 3 adds the position section's pin, one ablation, one changeset sentence, and "each section" in the README sentence.

## The PM's hypotheses, measured

1. **Partly refuted as worded.** The verdict did not gate "only the app's home route". It was asked only on `requestedAppMissing`, and that branch excludes every pseudo-route (`isSpecialRoute`): `create-app`, any `system` or `metadata` path segment, and the whole `/apps/setup` subtree (`isSetupRoute`).
   - For an ordinary app, every nested route already waited on the verdict. For Setup, no route did, the root included.
   - The metadata-admin routes are mounted in `AppContent` itself, in both route tables: the with-app branch's nested `metadata` route and the no-app branch's flat `metadata/...` routes. So the verdict belongs there, and `setupApp.ts` (Setup's identity constants) is untouched.
   - Why `/apps/setup` landed on the CRM dashboard: a pseudo-route falls back to the default launcher app, so the index route `AppRootLanding` navigated to CRM's first navigation entry, relative to the URL segment `setup`. That gave `/apps/setup/dashboard/pipeline_dashboard`.
2. **Narrowed, at the stop the dispatch provided for.** A route-tree gate over every `/apps/APP/...` route would hide pages that a member legitimately reaches under the Setup segment:
   - the approvals inbox at `/apps/setup/system/approvals`. The server's approval notifications carry `actionUrl: '/system/approvals'` and `'/system/approvals?request=ID'` (objectstack `plugin-approvals`, `approval-service.ts`), and `SystemRedirect` forwards `/system/*` onto `/apps/setup/system/*`;
   - the records that inbox opens, at `/apps/setup/OBJECT/record/ID` (`ApprovalsInboxPage`'s `recordHref`, which falls back to `setup`);
   - `system/profile`, which lives in the same host route fragment.

   So the gate covers Setup's root and the metadata-admin routes. Those carry all three of the card's pages: the permission-set list, the permission-set editor and the position editor. The rest of the Setup subtree is left as a product decision, raised in the report. A caller the app admits sees no change: Setup is in their list, so the gate is not reached and nothing is probed. This is pinned, and was measured in the browser as admin.
3. **Confirmed and done.** See the Assigned Users bullets above.
4. **Serial.** PR #12731 landed as `c7462e7` and is merged into this branch cleanly. Both intents are kept: its named-record-page route sits in the with-app table, and this gate returns above that table. PR #12662 landed as `c41ce3f`, this branch's base. `setupApp.ts` is untouched.

## Tests (run at `57e9915`)

New pins:
- `packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/AppContent.setupItemRoutesVerdict-12706.test.tsx`: 11 cases. A real `ObjectStackAdapter` runs over a stubbed `fetch`, and the 403 body is the one the real by-name route sent for the member in the browser reading below.
  - A refused caller gets `app-access-denied` on the permission-set editor, the position editor, a metadata list, the metadata directory, Setup's root and a legacy metadata spelling. No page stub mounts (each stub counts its mounts), there is exactly one probe and it names `setup`, and the URL is left as typed.
  - Another refused app's metadata route gets the same verdict, so this is the app's own verdict and not a Setup rule.
  - CONTROLS: an admitted caller gets the editor under Setup's chrome with no probe. A 404 (a server with no such app) renders as before. The approvals inbox and the record page it links to stay reachable for a refused caller.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/AssignedUsersSection.readRefused-12706.test.tsx`: 3 cases, also through a real `ObjectStackAdapter` over a stubbed `fetch`. The 403 body is the one the data route sent in the card's measurement.
  - A 403 holders read shows the refusal, and neither the empty copy nor a count.
  - CONTROL: a 200 empty read shows the empty copy and the count "0", with no alert.
  - A refused Remove says so, and the row stays.

Local runs, all at `57e9915`:
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over 189 files: every test file that names `AppContent`'s routes (all of `packages/app-shell/src/console/`, plus `apps/console`'s `AppContent.*`, `SetupRoute` and approvals-inbox ref suites) and every test naming `AssignedUsersSection`, `PositionHoldersSection` or the section's copy. Result: `Test Files  189 passed (189)`, `Tests  1279 passed (1279)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. `--listFiles` shows both new test files in the test project.
- Builds: the `@object-ui/app-shell` closure (`turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'`), 28/28 tasks. Then `@object-ui/console`, 35/35 tasks.

## Tests (round 3, run at `64dfb2e`)

- `PositionHoldersSection.readRefused-12706.test.tsx` alone: `Tests  2 passed (2)`.
- Seven files in one run: the new pin, `PositionHoldersSection.test.tsx`, `ResourceEditPage.setupCatalog-7611`, `setupHoldersGrant-12082`, plugin-form's `affordanceGrantMap-12082`, `AssignedUsersSection.readRefused-12706` and `AppContent.setupItemRoutesVerdict-12706`. Result: `Test Files  7 passed (7)`, `Tests  92 passed (92)`.
- Type-check, eslint (0 errors; the source's warnings went from 15 to 11), changeset presence and new line citations: all exit 0.

## Ablations (one per pin family, each through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`)

The subject resolves to source: the pins import `../AppContent`, `./AssignedUsersSection` and `./PositionHoldersSection` relatively, so no `dist/` leg applies. Each mutation was proven on disk (anchor count 1 to 0, blob changed). Each restore was proven by the blob equalling HEAD's and `git diff HEAD` being empty.
- **Route gate:** `appSurfaceAwaitsVerdict` forced to `false`. Result: 7 failed, 4 passed. Every refused-caller pin went red, and the 4 controls stayed green.
- **Read failure:** `setReadFailure(...)` in the read's `catch` replaced with `setReadFailure(null)`. Result: 1 failed, 2 passed. The 403 pin went red; the 200-empty control and the Remove pin stayed green.
- **Refused Remove:** the `setError(...)` in Remove's `catch` deleted. Result: 1 failed, 2 passed. Only the Remove pin went red.
- **Position read failure (round 3):** `setReadFailure({ said: refusalSentence(err) })` in the read's `catch` replaced with `setReadFailure(null)`. Result: 1 failed, 1 passed. The 403 pin went red; the 200-empty control stayed green.

## Browser reading

Backend: objectstack `66d456d01`, `examples/app-crm`, `objectstack dev --seed-admin --fresh`. Console: this branch at `57e9915`, Vite dev, 1280 × 900. The member was created by the admin (`POST /api/v1/auth/admin/create-user` answered 200) and changed their password. `GET /api/v1/auth/me/permissions` answered `permissionSets: ["member_default"]` and `systemPermissions: []`. `GET /api/v1/meta/app/setup` answered 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` for the member and 200 for the admin.

| page | member (no `setup.access`) | admin |
|---|---|---|
| `/apps/setup` | access-denied, URL stays, 0 headers | Setup landing (`dashboard/system_overview`) |
| `/apps/setup/metadata/permission?scope=environment` | access-denied | the list |
| `.../metadata/permission/crm_sales_user?scope=environment` | access-denied; no `sys_user_permission_set` read sent | the editor; Assigned Users "0" and the empty copy after a 200 empty read |
| `.../metadata/position/sales_rep?scope=environment` | access-denied; no `sys_user_position` read sent | the editor |
| `/apps/setup/system/approvals` | the Approvals Inbox, unchanged | the inbox |
| `/apps/crm_app` | the CRM dashboard, unchanged | CRM |

The refused-read state can no longer be reached by the card's member, because the gate stops them before the editor. It was read as admin with `page.route` answering the holders `GET` with the server's 403 body. That response is ROUTED (stubbed in the browser); everything rendering it is the real console. The section showed "Assigned Users", Add user, and the alert "You do not have permission to perform this action. Contact your administrator if you need access.", with no count and no "No users assigned yet".

Round 3, at `64dfb2e`, same backend, as admin, at `.../metadata/position/sales_rep?scope=environment`. With the server's own answer (`GET sys_user_position` 200), the section showed "Position holders" with "0" and "Nobody holds this position yet.", and no alert. With the holders `GET` ROUTED to the server's 403 body (stubbed in the browser, real console), it showed "Position holders" with no count and the alert "You do not have permission to perform this action. Contact your administrator if you need access.", and no empty copy.

In dev, the probe went out twice per page load. The console mounts under `React.StrictMode` (`apps/console/src/main.tsx`), which runs effects twice in dev; the unit pins, rendered without StrictMode, count exactly one.

## Acceptance notes

- **The rest of the Setup subtree is not gated, and not filed** (the seat's scope note `6220857048`). For a caller Setup refuses, `component/...`, object lists, dashboards and `system/*` other than approvals and profile still render under the default app's chrome, and the server still refuses their data. This is read from code only, and no producer links a member there, so it does not pass the filing gate today. Three shapes are recorded, and the seat rules on none of them:
  - **A.** Stop at this PR's scope.
  - **B.** Gate the whole subtree except a console allowlist (`system/approvals`, `system/profile`, `OBJECT/record/ID`). That would be a second access rule in the console, which this card's claim forbids.
  - **C.** Move the member-facing links off the Setup segment at their producers (`SystemRedirect` targets the caller's own app segment; the inbox's `recordHref` drops its `setup` fallback), then gate the subtree on Setup's verdict.
  - If a refused-caller page beyond these is measured, it is filed then, as a decision card with these options.
- **Package-id URL (carrier: objectui#12285).** `/apps/com.objectstack.setup/metadata/...` asks the probe with the package id. objectui#12285 is the by-name route answering 404 for that, which reads as `not_found` and so renders as before. This was read from the code, not measured in the browser. Once objectui#12285's probe resolves package ids, this gate covers that spelling with no change here.
- **The objectui#4473 bounce.** A member whose app list is empty and who opens `/apps/setup` now gets the access-denied screen, with its Back to home button, when Setup's verdict is `denied`. Before, they were redirected home. The provider no longer produces the stale-cache arrival that motivated the bounce (objectui#4486), so what remains is a typed URL or bookmark, and the verdict screen is the honest answer to it. `AppContent.inaccessibleAppStrand.test.tsx` uses an adapter without the probe (`unknown`) and stays green.
- **`PositionHoldersSection` is changed in this PR** (round 3, after the claim's re-statement `6220867274`), with the same refusal state as `AssignedUsersSection`. `AssignedUsersSection`'s Add path still reads its refusal through the old key chain (`err.body.error`, `err.error`, `err.message`). That is an observation, not a defect measured here: the ObjectStack client sets `message`, which the chain's third arm reads.
